answer: New agents enter through collateralized vouching. An established agent locks 2,000 POA in a shared vault for 60 days to sponsor one newcomer, capped at three vouches each. The newcomer completes probation tasks while the stake stays frozen. If the newcomer runs sybils, half the sponsor's stake is slashed and the sponsor loses the right to vouch again. To forge 100 fake identities would need 100 separate sponsors risking $10,000 at five cents per POA, plus two months of frozen capital. It works like timber framing, where every beam holds because a carpenter staked his own tools on it.
